guide: This post is about building a small app around something you already love, so other people use it. You need ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code, a free Vercel account and a free Supabase account.
1. Pick one interest you already care about and write one sentence on who else cares about it and what they would use an app for.
1. Ask ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code to turn that sentence into a plan for the smallest app that does one useful thing.
1. Have the assistant build a simple web app with a Next.js front end, using Supabase for sign-in and a database for each user's saved items.
1. Run the app on your own computer and click through it yourself, fixing anything that breaks before anyone else sees it.
1. Deploy it to Vercel so it has a public link.
1. Send the link to a few people who share the interest and ask what they would change.
1. Make the changes they ask for, one at a time, and redeploy.
Watch out: build for a niche you actually belong to, because people only sign up for apps that speak to them, and don't launch with more than one feature.

```
You are my coding assistant. Help me build a small web app for people who share this interest: <my interest>. The app should do one useful thing: <the single thing users should be able to do>. I'm not a developer, so explain each step in plain English before you do it.
Tools I have: <ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code>, a free Vercel account and a free Supabase account.
Build it with Next.js and TypeScript, using Supabase for email sign-in and a table that stores each user's saved items. Keep to one feature and one screen to start. Do not add extras I haven't asked for.
Constraints: keep all secret keys in environment variables, never in the code. Use Supabase row-level security so each user can only see their own data. Keep the design simple and mobile friendly.
Return: a short build plan, the full project code, the exact commands to run it locally, the Supabase table and security setup, and the steps to deploy it to Vercel. Finish with a list of three things I should test before sharing the link.
```
Skipped: nothing checked against live pages. Risk: the source never names the stack Manraj used, so the Next.js, Supabase and Vercel choices are my suggestion rather than his.
